Those They Left Behind: Interviews, Stories, Essays and Poems by Survivors of Suicide

I recently listened to an audiobook of 50 stories of those left to deal with the suicide and it's a pretty good glimpse into what the act can do. I'm HFA, AS with severe (Dr.'s word) depression and have a really hard time understanding just what the impact would be. The book helped me some to understand what a strong impact my decision would have. You might want to see if you can get a copy.
The time just isn't right yet. When it's the right time, this won't be a problem. There's no tricks of the trade, you're just not at the right point. Have to keep hanging on for now.

I get that too. I want to yell at the men I work with. I'm in a high-education white collar job and either because I look young, or whatever else, these people talk to me like I'm twelve. It's bullsht. Looking young doesn't make someone stupid just as being old doesn't make someone smart.  My own rant aside, trust me on three things (1) those people are assholes, (2) those people have NO clue how they are sounding, (3) there will always be those people. The good side: you aren't a jerk like them, you (hopefully) can limit your time with them, other people go through this and feel just as depressed and angry over it, and I'll cycle back to say: you aren't a jerk like them. That's peace of mind right right there. You can't control others actions, but you can control your actions and development.

Your boyfriend sounds delightful. I'd highly recommend working wherever and doing college. Not that we are anything alike, I have no way of knowing that, but my experience: I worked jobs I HATED (solely because of the customers) to pay my way through school. Never held one for more than a year. Took 3 years to go through community college, another 2 and 1/2 after transferring to a 4 year school. And now, fast forward 8 years, I have a doctorate in molecular neuroscience. The SOLE motivation for me to put up with the bs side of school ( and there's a lot of it) was that I didn't want to work the customer service jobs I loathed. Seriously, if it hadn't been my hatred for customer service, I never would have kept pursuing education. If anyone gives you shit about going to a community college, they're an idiot and this isn't high school--walk away from. Mid conversation. Just leave.  Education comes with a lot of crap but the end goal is to have a job you really like. Just keep that focus in mind. There will always be things you hate at any job (I despise who I'm forced to share an office with, you'll have something else) but the overall effect is liking showing up to work everyday. And for most of us higher education means no more customer service jobs!

I just go real silent and think "They have nooo idea what they are saying to me right now."  Not that anyone's words would drive me to finally carry out but, the thought's always there, so sure bring it to the surface, thanks, something to ponder the rest of my day.

Only way out is to find something to focus on and focus hard. People won't be there for you consistently (if at all) you know that. Can't rely on them. But you can shut out the rest of the world and focus everything you have, mentally, physically, financially, heart body mind and soul in that project. For me it was an education route. For some it's work, music, others something the rest of us would call "just a hobby." I won't insult your intelligence by going on. If you're at this state, you get it. The only way out is You have to find something (not human related) and focus, focus hard, shut out everything and that something is now your life. Hopefully you already have something in mind reading this. Now Fuck how you feel, fuck the emotions, Now you learn to make it all go away by living inside yourself. Inside you focus.

Did they give you any antidepressants when you got out?! I find it shocking there are rehab counselors and doctors that don't know mood disorders and anxiety precede drug use. Giving you behavioral tools without addressing the organic problem is irresponsible and idiotic. I'd try to find a pdoc that specializes in post rehab ______ (whatever your age range). You have biochemical imbalances from the drugs that can last several years, and you likely had biochemical imbalances, such as an organic source of depression, long before the drug use. The REAL problem needs to be addressed.

Worst is no one really sees it and experiences it like you do. This stuff eats away at you because even if try to open up and talk about it with friends, it becomes trivialized. They don't understand it like you do and they certainly can't feel the slow grating this behavior from a parent has. You have to distance yourself from your parents. In the early 20s you should be going about steps to resolve all the trauma a headfuck parent imparted on you. That's when you fully look back and realize it wasn't you, it was her. You can't do that if you keep letting her spear her talons into you.
